explain.say: Help can come from people and from things. You can ask a person, Can you show me? You can say, I am stuck here. Things can help too, like a word mat, a dictionary or an example. Today, ask for help one time.

faq.a: No. Asking for help is how everyone learns, even grown-ups and experts. Cheating is copying answers. Asking is learning.

faq.q: What can I say when I need help?
faq.a: You can say, Can you show me, please? or I am stuck on this part, or What does this word mean?
asks: Tell me about Ask for help
Tell me about Ask a person

faq.a: Look at examples, word mats, pictures, a dictionary or your notes. These are helpers too.
asks: Tell me about Look for clues

faq.a: Trying first shows you what you know and exactly where you are stuck. Then your helper knows how to help.

faq.q: What if I feel embarrassed to ask?
faq.a: Lots of people feel that. You can ask quietly, or write a note. A grown-up you trust will want to help.

facts: Astronauts on the International Space Station work closely with teams on the ground who help them.
Asking a question helps you learn exactly the part you are stuck on.

quiz.say: Kofi tried and checked the example. He is still stuck. What can he say?
quiz.show: Kofi is still stuck. What can he say?
quiz.why: Kofi tried first and looked for clues. Now asking for help is the next step.

wrong.0: Kofi can still learn this, with a little help.
wrong.1: A guess can be wrong, and asking helps him understand.

quiz.say: Mei asks her teacher to explain a word. What is Mei doing?
quiz.show: Mei asks about a word. What is Mei doing?
quiz.why: Asking about a word helps Mei understand it. That is learning.

wrong.0: Cheating is copying answers, and Mei is asking to understand.
wrong.2: Mei is still working on it, so she has kept going.
